headline: Ludicrous $999 Steam game lasts just 10 minutes and offers a 'golden ticket' achievement
summary: This 'most expensive game on Steam' is a first-person luxury experience designed for conspicuous consumption, awarding a unique achievement to buyers.
details: A curious new PC game titled "Congratulations On Your Purchase" has appeared on Steam, priced at $999. It proudly claims to be "the most expensive game on Steam."

Buyers who purchase and run the title will experience a "first-person luxury experience set inside a palace." The main draw is collecting a 'golden ticket' Steam Achievement, signifying their membership among the elite.
Despite the premium price, the gameplay lasts only about 10 minutes. The developers' Steam sales pitch states, "The price is not a mistake. It is the point."

The game targets those compelled by conspicuous consumption, with the description adding, "You paid for this. Not accidentally. Not on impulse. You saw the price. You read the description. And then you bought it anyway. Welcome."

Developed by Minimum Viable Prestige and published by Worth It Studio, this concept echoes the $999 "I Am Rich" iOS app from the noughties. So far, two buyers have reportedly left personalized messages on the game's in-game wall.

headline: Get a 4TB SSD for $399 this Prime Day — 9.7 cents per GB is as good as it gets
summary: Team Group's T-Force G50 M.2 drive is now available for $399, making it the cheapest 4TB SSD on the market. This deal comes amidst rising SSD prices due to AI component shortages.
details: The Team Group T-Force G50 M.2 drive is currently the cheapest 4TB SSD available, priced at $399. This deal offers a significant $120 saving on its list price, making it a standout offer during Prime Day.
To secure the $399 price, the drive is listed at Newegg for $449 after an initial $70 discount. An additional $50 saving can be applied using the promo code FTTF462 at checkout.

This is a Gen 4 PCIe 4.0 SSD, offering sequential read speeds up to 5,000 Mbps and write speeds up to 4,500 Mbps. While not Gen 5 speeds, it includes a patented graphene heat-sink for cooling and easier installation.

The $399 price point, equating to roughly 9.7 cents per GB, is considered excellent value given the current market. AI component shortages have driven SSD prices up, and some industry experts suggest the retail SSD market is shrinking, making such deals increasingly rare.
